title: Closed ideal quotients of complete normed algebras
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with an absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$: $|\lambda|=0\Leftrightarrow\lambda=0$, $|\lambda\mu|=|\lambda||\mu|$ and $|\lambda+\mu|\le|\lambda|+|\mu|$ (a normed field). Let $R$ be a commutative unital $K$-algebra with a complete norm satisfying $\|x\|=0\Leftrightarrow x=0$, $\|-x\|=\|x\|$, $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$, $\|xy\|\le\|x\|\|y\|$ and $\|\lambda x\|=|\lambda|\|x\|$. Let $I\subset R$ be an ideal closed for the metric $\|x-y\|$. On the quotient algebra $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] put $N(\bar x)=\inf_{z\in I}\|x+z\|$. This is independent of the representative $x$, and is a complete norm satisfying $N(u)=0\Leftrightarrow u=0$, $N(-u)=N(u)$, $N(u+v)\le N(u)+N(v)$, $N(uv)\le N(u)N(v)$ and $N(\lambda u)=|\lambda|N(u)$. The ideal $I=R$ and the resulting zero quotient are allowed.
